elements.evidence: Section 13 as rendered still binds both parties: "Neither party shall, for twelve (12) months after the end of such personnel's involvement with the Services, solicit for hire ... any of the other party's personnel". Customer (Company) therefore remains subject to a non-solicit; the preferred position would require deletion of the clause as to Customer.

Retained opening words "Neither party shall ... solicit ... any of the other party's personnel" apply symmetrically to Company and Contractor; the added carve-out sentence is likewise drafted by reference to "the other party's personnel" and so operates for both sides.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Retained scope language limits the covered group to "any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services"; no residual reference to all employees or personnel generally survives in Section 13.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: The original temporal anchor "during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination" is replaced with "for twelve (12) months after the end of such personnel's involvement with the Services", which is exactly the individual-involvement anchor the fallback requires (deterministic check "non-solicit duration \u2264 12 months" ok).

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: New second sentence: "The foregoing restriction does not apply to general advertisements or other solicitations not specifically directed at the other party's personnel"; carve-out check reported present.

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Same inserted sentence ends "... or to unsolicited approaches by such personnel", expressly excluding unsolicited candidate approaches from the restriction.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative verb remains solicitation-only "solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise"; there is no free-standing no-hire, "employ or engage" or "induce ... to leave" prohibition anywhere in the rendered clause, so hiring absent solicitation is not barred.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback level: all six fallback elements are met in operative language (mutuality and involvement-based scope were already present; the duration re-anchor and the two carve-outs are delivered by the inserted text, not merely promised in the comment).
Preferred is not met and the finding does not claim it: Customer remains bound by a non-solicit. To reach preferred the drafter would have to delete Section 13's application to Company entirely.

Minimality holds. Only the defective temporal phrase ("during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination") was replaced, and a single carve-out sentence was added; favourable retained language (the express-written-consent mechanic with the not-unreasonably-withheld qualifier, the direct-involvement scope limit, the solicitation-only verb) survives untouched. No survival tail, expense language, remedy or other extras were introduced.

The phrase "or other solicitations not specifically directed at the other party's personnel" is the customary operative definition of the general-advertisement carve-out rather than a separate new requirement, so it does not breach minimality.

Intent preserved: no undefined terms, dangling cross-references or contradictory retained sentences; "Services" and "personnel" carry their existing meanings and the consent mechanic still functions with the new period.

Observation only (not a defect): because the period now runs from the end of an individual's involvement, the clause is arguably silent during ongoing involvement. That is Customer-favourable and outside the checklist, so it is not flagged.
